title: Gut microbiota varies by opioid use, circulating leptin and oxytocin in African American men with diabetes and high burden of chronic disease

what_it_measured.text: Abstract Objective The gut microbiota is known to be related to type 2 diabetes (T2D), psychiatric conditions, and opioid use.
This study was a part of the Glucose tolerance and vitamin D in African American Male veterans (GluDAAM) cohort study that evaluated glucose metabolism biomarkers in AAM.

Samples were pooled in equimolar ratio and quantified using a Qubit 2.0 fluorometer.

Oxytocin was measured in a clean catch urine sample at the University of Wisconsin-Madison’s Wisconsin National Primate Research Center (WNPRC) with Assay Design ELISA kits (Enzo Life Sciences, Ann Arbor, MI) [22].

reported_results.text: Results The study subjects had prevalent overweight/obesity (78%), T2D (50%) and co-morbid psychiatric (65%) and opioid use (45%) disorders.
Results Bio-clinical subject characteristics Assessment of all subjects showed high rate of smoking (35%), opioid use (45%), and overweight/obesity (78%).
Contrary, there was no significant difference in Bifidobacterium when comparing opioid users with non-users in individuals taking metformin (log2FC = 0.53, p = 0.51, q = 0.88) (Fig 5B).
The opposite trends were observed for the order Lactobacillales, a higher abundance in High-Leptin compared to Low-Leptin subgroup (p = 0.06) and vice versa for oxytocin (p = 0.05) (Fig 7).
Contrary, there was higher abundance of Dialister in High-Oxytocin compared to Low-Oxytocin subgroup (p = 0.04).
There was lower abundance of Dialister in High-Leptin compared to Low-Leptin subgroup (p = 0.03).
